sources.supports: Every method validates its identifier and places it as the only path segment of the matching endpoint. The list step converts the isCompleted and isStarted booleans to the 1 and 0 TestRail reads and sends neither when they are absent. The reads and the two writes parse against MilestoneSchema; the delete passes no schema and resolves with no value. No payload is parsed by a public method, so every milestone payload rule is enforced at the MCP boundary alone.

get_milestones takes is_completed and is_started, each 1 or 0, plus limit and offset from TestRail 6.7. add_milestone requires name and accepts description, due_on, start_on, parent_id and refs, with parent_id from TestRail 5.3 and refs from 6.4. update_milestone supports partial updates; its own table lists is_completed, is_started, parent_id and start_on, while the endpoint accepts the add fields too. Deleting a milestone cannot be undone. No field is documented as clearable by null.

input_policy.notes: The endpoint takes one identifier in the path and no request body at all, so every field beyond it is refused.

outer_result.notes: The method resolves with no value and the wrapper reports data: null. TestRail's reference states only that deleting a milestone cannot be undone. It does not say what becomes of the milestone's sub-milestones, which the entity carries under its milestones field, nor of the runs and plans that pointed at it, and neither does the driver; the tool therefore claims neither, because a blast radius no cited source states is not one this manifest can promise.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Send exactly one request. The adapter never follows up with further calls to find or repair what the deletion removed.

parameters.semantics: The milestone to delete. No coercion; passed positionally and sent verbatim as the only path segment.

wire.encoding: Decimal integer path segment; numeric strings are rejected rather than coerced.
